findings.reason: the section must scope the reset to the three trees (`reset_to_status(..., extra_filter=...)` already supports it) or state the facility-wide consequence, otherwise the first implementer burns the whole facility's scoring to repair one root.
findings.text: the section runs `discover paths jt-60sa --reset-to scanned --root /analysis/src` as though `--root` scopes the reset to that tree, but the CLI calls `reset_to_status(spec, facility)` with no `extra_filter` (`imas_codex/cli/discover/paths.py:247`), so `--root` is applied only to the subsequent discovery run and the reset hits every jt-60sa path whose status is `triaged` or `scored` (source_statuses at `imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:250-251`) — the plan's own §1 measures 3,778 scored, all of which would return to `scanned` for a full re-triage and re-score at LLM cost

findings.reason: the mechanism the section depends on is unverified against the code and may be a no-op, so the section must clear `expanded_at` (or verify it is null for that row) before relying on the reset, else the done-when cannot be met by the command it names.
findings.text: the section asserts that resetting the `/analysis/src` row to `scanned` "re-lists it and creates child rows through persist_scan_results", but re-listing is done by `claim_paths_for_expanding`, which requires `expanded_at IS NULL` (`imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:547-549`), and `PATH_RESET_SPECS["scanned"]` clears triage/enrich/score fields but not `expanded_at` (`imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:251-256`), so if `/analysis/src` was previously expanded the reset → triage → expand cycle never fires and the three trees stay unlisted

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §19 hides one expression (`coalesce` source-path) behind a single rendered-fragment function used by three sites, and §14 adds no module at all, so neither section spreads complexity over shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §14 reuses `imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py` (the reset owner) rather than forking a re-list path, and §19 explicitly keeps the `HAS_CHUNK` edge with its single writer (`imas_codex/ingestion/pipeline.py:522`) and consolidates the duplicated `coalesce` into one fragment rather than adding a second link pass.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §14 adds no CLI option (it reuses the existing `--reset-to`/`--root`) and §19 states "Interface budget: nothing added" and names the two inlined copies the fragment replaces, so neither section adds surface without accounting for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §14 cites the existing `PATH_RESET_SPECS["scanned"]` reset to re-list `/analysis/src`, but the code shows the cited mechanism does not behave as the plan claims (unscoped reset; `expanded_at` not cleared), so the plan's account of the prior art is wrong on the point the section rests on.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §19's fragment helper is the repo's existing `build_*_predicate(alias)` convention (`parallel.py::build_enrich_claimable_predicate`, `build_category_predicate`), justified as consolidating two inlined copies and pinned by a test; §14 adds no layer over the reset CLI.
